reviews.title: New update shoots the app and site in the foot
reviews.text: They will now essentially be tracking the notes of each comment on a reblog chain as a separate post. You might make a post that gets five reblogs, but one of them had a comment attached that got a thousand. Some of those reblogs would splinter into their own chains. You would not be notified of any of this, and would only find out if you dug through the rabbit hole yourself for some reason—because only five reblogs came directly from your version of the post. On a site where word-of-mouth is the most common way for a post to spread (nearly all users opt out of the algorithm) and long post chains with all the notes headed back to the original poster are a keystone of site culture, this is a very very bad move. It’s also A) terrible for artists—we now have no idea how far a post is actually spreading unless we carefully investigate each one. We love to see feedback and comments on our work, and we’ll see way less of those now even on the off chance a post goes viral. B) Extremely unsafe. If someone posts a selfie, and a comment-reblog or two happens, now the original poster isn’t notified about what people are saying. An image of yourself could circulate among god-knows who saying god-knows what and you won’t find out about it, and even if you do deleting your version of the post won’t help. It’s making the site and app worse on all fronts.

reviews.title: Consistently Getting Worse, Especially Now
reviews.text: Tumblr has been through some ups and downs over the years; it’s thankfully one of the only social media sites left that isn’t algorithm driven, and I’ve found some real communities on here, but the current direction they’re taking the site and app seems almost purposely designed to burn all of that down. The most recent change, which reworks the reblog system into a ripoff of Twitter’s quote retweets, destroys the fundamental way in which users talk and interact on the site (communicating back and forth via reblogs), steals engagement from creators, enables harassment (posters are no longer notified of what goes on on their own posts, and turning off reblogs effectively doesn’t work anymore), and undermines the entire culture that makes Tumblr so special. The fact that the developers even brought this idea this far is worrying - it proves that they at the very least don’t understand how or why people use their app and site - the fact that they’re pushing it so hard and not immediately reverting it speaks volumes. I am genuinely considering leaving what has been my main social media site for almost a decade, and I can’t in good conscious recommed a platform that is so determined to destroy itself and its user base.

reviews.title: Absolutely Terrible Update
reviews.text:
The recent update changing the reblog system has made the website a genuinely miserable place for me, and other artists, writers and creators who have used this platform for years. 

So many creatives rely on this platform for both self expression, community, and promoting their work for business prospects, but because people are much more likely to reblog from whoever they saw the post from, it is nearly impossible for creatives to receive traction for their work they mace. 

This is highly discouraging for me, and for thousands of other artists. This platform was a place where I found a lot of my online friends throughout the years, but until the reblog system changes back to the way it was, I don’t see myself using Tumblr going forward.

reviews.title: New Update is Horrible
reviews.text:
I’ve been on Tumblr for several years, using it as my main social media site. I really liked how cozy it felt compared to other very algorithmic websites and apps. I don’t scroll endlessly, because there is an end, which is why I kept coming back. However, this new update has just thrown so much of that community out of the window. 
Other updates to “modernize” the site and make it more like tiktok or instagram or twitter have been mostly avoidable features, but this one is not. The notes feature has been changed and now it is easier than ever to harass and start hate campaigns on other users, or to prevent an artist or creative from getting credit from their work. If you have ever seen someone get “ratioed” on another platform, even if the original post is good and deserving of that engagement, well, now that is entirely possible on Tumblr as well, something that I absolutely despise. 
Even worse, the official account made a post introducing the new update, got unprecedented negative feedback on it, and then said the equivalent of “too bad, so sad, we’re not reverting the changes.” Absolutely despicable of Tumblr. Extremely disappointing and I no longer plan on using Tumblr besides on my computer with a heavy duty adblocker. I will be deleting this app from my phone until this change is reverted. This is a horrific example of corporations deciding what people can get, and I won’t be supporting them anymore.

They’ve completely changed the interactions features to now actively remove support and interaction from artists and clog the UI even more- which I thought wouldn’t be possible after they added the useless reels feature that no one likes or uses. It’s hard to explain how monumentally bad this update is without seeing it yourself, but I would not recommend it. Anyone looking to download or use this app since this recent update should just find somewhere else.
